newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-GALTHIE RETURNS AGAINST IRELAND.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-GALTHIE RETURNS AGAINST IRELAND.

text.p: Scrum-half Fabien Galthie has been recalled to a familiar-looking French team to play Ireland in their opening Five Nations championship match in Dublin on Saturday.
Galthie was widely expected to play after coach Jean-Claude Skrela decided to do without Guy Accoceberry, lacklustre in France's second test defeat to South Africa in November.

With Olivier Roumat and Philippe Saint-Andre out of action with injuries, Skrela has retained Toulouse lock Hugues Miorin and Brive winger David Venditti, generally sticking to the choices made against the Springboks late last year.

Even though the French have slightly reshuffled their back-row, restoring Fabien Pelous to number eight with captain Abdel Benazzi and Philippe Benetton on the flanks, the main change has been the arrival of assistant coach Pierre Villepreux.
"I'm especially looking after the backs. In two days of training I've had time to adapt to the frame of mind in this squad," said Villepreux.
"As for Jean-Claude's gameplans, I knew them already. They are exactly the same as the ones I have."
Skrela explained he wanted Villepreux to help France eradicate some of their weaknesses, especially in keeping the ball in hand.
"This season, what we need to work on is not losing the ball and being able to keep it in play," Skrela said.
"I don't want to see any aimless up-and-unders either. We must be consistent."
Despite Ireland's recent 37-29 loss to Italy, Skrela warned his troops against overconfidence in Dublin.
"We must not underrate them. It would be a gross mistake to take them lightly. They are a team with qualities and especially a lot of spirit," he said.

15-Jean-Luc Sadourny; 14-Emile Ntamack, 13-Richard Dourthe, 12-Thomas Castaignede, 11-David Venditti; 10-Alain Penaud, 9-Fabien Galthie; 8-Fabien Pelous, 7-Philippe Benetton, 6-Abdel Benazzi (captain), 5-Hugues Miorin, 4-Olivier Merle, 3-Franck Tournaire, 2-Marc Dal Maso, 1-Christian Califano.
